v1.19.0 closes the 1.18 series, and the series was one capability: a graph that holds several
companies now reports them as a group. Each company keeps its own books, chart, calendar and close;
a consolidation entity holds the entries that turn their sum into the group's statements; an engine
computes those entries from the books; and the group closes its month as one more close, after its
companies have closed theirs, with the consolidated statements stamped like any company's. Around it
came the accounting the group statements need from every company: an equity statement that rolls
forward, a cash flow that handles the entries that move no cash, opening balances, and rows a tenant
can add to its own statements.

Covers everything since v1.18.0; the 1.18.x patches carried generated changelogs. It also carries
the fixes from a review of the whole series before this release, listed at the end.

## A group in one graph

**Treatment and membership.** An entity now says how the group treats it and for which months it
belonged. `consolidation_method` is `full`, `equity`, `cost` or `none`, derived from
`ownership_pct` unless given (half or more consolidates in full, a fifth to a half takes the equity
method, less is an investment at cost). `entity_role` is `operating` or `consolidation`, and
`joined_on` / `left_on` bound the membership by month. `create-entity` and `update-entity` take all
four.

**Two group scopes.** `live-financial-statement` takes `scope`: `entity`, `combined` or
`consolidated`. `combined` sums the parent and the members consolidated in full, each for the months
it was a member, with nothing eliminated. `consolidated` adds the consolidation entity, so its
eliminations and noncontrolling interest are summed in. An equity-method or cost member is never
summed; the group carries its investment and its share of the member's result instead. The combined
sum merges rows on the Style's presentation order, so a row only one entity has lands where the
Style puts it.

**The consolidation worksheet.** `consolidation-worksheet` lays one window of the group's statement
out by entity: the parent, each member in full, their combined sum, the consolidation entity's
adjustments, the consolidated total, and each equity-method or cost member beside the sum, never in
it. It reads the ledger live, over REST and as an MCP tool.

**The rows a group needs, in every Reporting Style.** Noncontrolling interest on the balance sheet
and the income statement, the parent's investment in its subsidiaries, balances due from and to
affiliates, the equity-method investment and its share of income, and a second roll-forward on the
equity statement for the noncontrolling interest: beginning balance, share of income, contributions,
distributions.

## The consolidation engine

`preview-consolidation-entries(period)` computes a month's consolidating entries from the books.
For each member consolidated in full, inside its membership:

- **the investment against the member's capital**, the parent's share eliminated against its
  investment and the outside owners' share as noncontrolling interest;
- **intercompany balances and charges**, matched by the entity each line's event names;
- **the outside owners' share of the month's result**;

and for each equity-method member, the parent's share of its result, with its distributions moved
against the investment.

Each proposal is the month's target less what the consolidation entity already holds of that kind
and member, so an entry posted by hand counts and is never reversed. A residual between the parent's
investment and its share of the member's capital is returned beside the proposals and withheld,
never plugged; a distribution the parent took as income explains it, and the engine reverses that
income with the elimination. Intercompany figures the two sides disagree on come back as reconciling
items. Each eliminating line carries the cash flow row it offsets, so the consolidated cash flow
nets the flows its members' own entries produced.

`propose-consolidation-entries(period)` writes the proposals as drafts in the consolidation entity,
replacing its own earlier drafts of the month and never a person's. `set-allocation-override`
records an outside owners' share other than their percentage for one month — a preferred return, a
waterfall — with its basis. Journal entries take `adjustment_kind` and `adjusts_entity_id`, accepted
only on the consolidation entity.

## The group close

The consolidation entity's close is the group close. It holds the month while an entity the month
consolidates has not closed it, while the consolidating entries are neither posted nor drafted,
while a residual or an intercompany disagreement is left, or while the consolidated balance sheet or
equity statement fails its checks. `get-fiscal-calendar` names each of these in the `group_*` lists,
and a refused close returns them. `allow_unexplained_residuals` closes over a residual and records
each one in the audit note. A member's month the group has closed reopens only after the group's.

The close stamps the month's consolidated statements as the consolidation entity's own, so every
reader that keys on an entity reads the group's closed statements by that entity's id, and the
parent's own stamp is untouched.

## The statements every company reads

**The equity statement rolls forward.** It opens on a beginning balance, moves through rows of its
own — stock issued and repurchased, dividends, contributions and distributions, share-based
compensation, other — filled from every equity line rather than only the ones that moved cash, and
is validated as a roll-forward: a column whose beginning balance plus changes misses its ending
balance fails.

**The cash flow handles what moves no cash.** An entry with no cash line no longer lands in the
reconciling adjustment: its income-statement part is backed out as a non-cash item and its
working-capital part out of that account's change. A payment that settles a bill for equipment or
loan principal is read through to the bill, so the cash lands in investing or financing. Gains,
losses and impairments are presented the standard indirect way. A supplemental section discloses
capital expenditures not yet paid, non-cash acquisitions, and cash paid for interest and for income
taxes. A payment that settles a bill it doesn't link to is named in the statement's warnings, and an
account mapped to more than one concept counts once.

**Opening balances.** `record-opening-balance` starts a company's books from a balance sheet: one
`opening` entry dated the day before its first fiscal month, which every month's opening balances
include and no month's activity does. It can be recorded again until the first close. A statement
column that reaches back before the books begin is left out of a live statement and carries only its
balances in a saved report, and `omitted_periods` names what was left out.

**Rows from the 10-Ks.** A coverage pass over recent 10-Ks in the SEC repository ranked the
face-statement rows filers use that the Reporting Styles lacked. Share-based compensation (as an
expense, a cash flow add-back and an equity movement) and professional fees are now in every Style.

**Style extensions.** A tenant can add rows to its own statements: a `reporting_extension` structure
that names `extends_network` layers its rows onto that Style network, and they render, sum, persist
in saved reports and export. A row must anchor where a statement subtotal sums it, and a tenant
concept placed as a row must refine an rs-gaap concept, whose traits and types it takes.

**The export.** Exported reports carry preferred labels, so a subtracted cash flow row shows at its
cash effect and the equity statement opens and closes on its balances in every format.

## Also in the series

- `informationBlockSummaries` (GraphQL) lists blocks as identities and counts in one query, for
  rails and pickers that don't need every block's envelope; `list-information-blocks` uses it in
  summary mode.
- The per-graph MCP instructions describe the group: which entity is the consolidation entity, which
  members are not summed, and which scope a question about the group reads.
- Report facts are stored one per context, a subtotal whose children net to zero renders, and the
  graph's units and precision follow the fact's unit.
- `bind-text-block` binds only an element its structure arranges.
- The technical documentation moved from the GitHub wiki into `docs/technical/`, published at
  robosystems.ai/docs/technical.

## Fixed before release

A review of the series before this release found these, all fixed here:

- **XBRL 2.1 export validity.** With preferred labels, the equity roll-forward presented its capital
  concept twice through the same locators, and the negated label role was used without declaring
  it. Exports validate again, and the tests now validate a package with Arelle.
- **Style extension authoring.** An extension's calculation arcs must sum a row the extension adds,
  once on the statement it extends; a refining concept takes its parent's balance and period type when the request leaves them
  out; and the extended network is set only through `extends_network`.
- **The group close.** An entry the engine could not compute holds the close even when residuals are
  overridden, and the preview reports it as `incomplete`. A graph keeps one consolidation entity.
  Once the group has closed a month, the consolidation entity keeps its role, membership dates may
  not move within the closed months, and a new member joins after them; a month the group reopens
  no longer counts as closed. A member that joins later no longer blanks the group's columns from
  before it joined.
- **The consolidated cash flow.** The consolidation entity's cash flow nets to nothing, so an
  elimination nothing offsets cannot move the group's net change in cash. A distribution the parent
  took as income is not counted twice. A first proposal's catch-up of earlier months posts untagged
  instead of as that month's flows, and an entry is tagged whole or not at all. A reversed
  consolidating entry is no longer counted as held, and an intercompany balance both entities hold
  on an account the consolidation entity lacks is named rather than left uneliminated.
- **A depreciated asset sold for cash** shows the cash received as its proceeds, not its cost.

## API surface changes

Additive, all in the generated SDK tier, so a client minor. The 1.18 patches already carried most of
it to the clients; the one field new in this release is `incomplete` on
`preview-consolidation-entries`.

- New operations: `consolidation-worksheet`, `preview-consolidation-entries`,
  `propose-consolidation-entries`, `set-allocation-override`, `record-opening-balance`, each also an
  MCP tool.
- New fields: `scope` on `live-financial-statement`; `consolidation_method`, `entity_role`,
  `joined_on` and `left_on` on entities; `adjustment_kind` and `adjusts_entity_id` on journal
  entries; `allow_unexplained_residuals` on `close-period`; the `group_*` lists on the fiscal
  calendar; `omitted_periods` on the live statement; `period_role` on statement rows;
  `extends_network` on taxonomy block structures; `informationBlockSummaries` in GraphQL.
- Behaviour: `bind-text-block` answers 422 for an element its structure does not arrange.
  `list-information-blocks` (MCP) summary rows carry `entity_id`, `fact_count` and
  `connection_count`, and no longer carry `disclosure_id`, `element_count`, `rule_count`,
  `has_fact_set` or `verification_result_count`.

Nothing in the SDK facades or the integration template's emit path changed.

## Deploying this release

- **No new migrations.** Extensions migrations `0046`–`0055` shipped with the 1.18 patches; a
  deployment coming from v1.18.11 has them all. One coming from earlier runs whichever it lacks.
- **No CloudFormation changes.**
- **Behaviour on existing data.** A group's live statements read under the fixed rules at once; a
  month the group has already closed keeps the statements it stamped until that month is reopened.
  A consolidation entity's open month may now show `incomplete` where an intercompany balance sits
  on an account its chart lacks: map an account to that concept on its chart and propose again.
